title: An Introduction to Machine Learning Methods for Fraud Detection
authors: Antonio Alessio Compagnino; Ylenia Maruccia; Stefano Cavuoti; Giuseppe Riccio; Antonio Tutone; Riccardo Crupi; Antonio Pagliaro
tldr: Comprehensive review of ML methods for financial fraud detection reveals supervised models like Random Forest achieve high accuracy but struggle with recall on imbalanced data, requiring hybrid approaches and explainable AI for real-world deployment.
problem_and_motivation: Financial fraud represents one of the most pressing challenges facing modern business sectors, with 56% of companies worldwide experiencing some form of fraud. Traditional detection approaches are increasingly inadequate for addressing contemporary threats. The sophistication and scale of fraudulent activities continue to evolve, rendering traditional detection approaches inadequate. This comprehensive review aims to provide a systematic analysis of ML techniques for financial fraud detection, addressing the current state of research and practical applications while bridging the gap between academic research and operational reality.
approach: Systematic literature review of over 120 peer-reviewed articles from 2014-2023.
Analysis of supervised, unsupervised, and hybrid learning approaches for fraud detection.
Two case studies applying supervised models to real-world banking data from Intesa Sanpaolo.
Examination of commonly used datasets including ULB2013, CSMAR, and synthetic datasets.
Evaluation of performance metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, AUC-ROC, AUPRC.
Analysis of fraud types: credit card, financial statement, insurance, money laundering, tax fraud.
findings: Random Forest most widely adopted (34 studies), achieving accuracy rates exceeding 95%.
XGBoost appears in 13 studies, particularly effective for imbalanced datasets.
Isolation Forest in 19 studies for anomaly detection without labeled data.
Autoencoders in 10 studies for dimensionality reduction and pattern capture.
LSTM in 8 studies for temporal sequence modeling in transaction data.
Class imbalance remains fundamental challenge with fraud rates <1% of transactions.
Case Study 1: Random Forest achieved AUPRC 0.619 but recall only 0.34 at default threshold.
Case Study 2: class_weight adjustments did not improve performance substantially.
Supervised methods alone insufficient for robust standalone deployment.
Hybrid approaches combining anomaly detection with supervised classification show promise.

Neural networks that learn to compress and reconstruct data, with reconstruction error serving as anomaly score.
Long Short-Term Memory networks designed to model temporal sequences and long-range dependencies in transaction data.
Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve - metric particularly valuable for imbalanced datasets where fraud is rare.
Phenomenon where model performance degrades as the relationship between features and fraud likelihood changes over time.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This review provides a comprehensive analysis of ML techniques for financial fraud detection, bridging theoretical knowledge with practical application through two case studies on proprietary banking data. The unique contribution lies in demonstrating that supervised models like Random Forest achieve high accuracy but critically fail on recall for minority fraud class, highlighting the need for hybrid architectures combining anomaly detection with supervised classification. The review establishes that class_weight adjustments are insufficient for severe imbalance, requiring data-level techniques like SMOTE or generative approaches.
directly_justifies: Random Forest achieves 95%+ accuracy but only 0.34 recall for fraud class.
Class imbalance with fraud rates <1% makes minority class learning extremely difficult.
Hybrid approaches combining anomaly detection with supervised classification show promise.
Federated learning enables privacy-preserving cross-institutional model training.
Explainable AI techniques like SHAP are essential for regulatory compliance.
limits: Focus exclusively on financial fraud detection excluding other fraud domains.
Case studies limited to Italian banking context may not generalize globally.
Literature review timeframe 2014-2023 may miss recent algorithmic advances.
Proprietary datasets from Intesa Sanpaolo limit reproducibility.
Supervised methods shown to be insufficient but alternatives require further validation.
Performance metrics may not capture all operational requirements in real-time systems.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all topic domains identified primary relevance in domains 6 (forecasting/evaluation), 8 (anomaly detection), and 10 (privacy). Domain 6.A is highly relevant through comprehensive review and application of ML forecasting algorithms. Domain 6.B is highly relevant for detailed analysis of evaluation metrics including AUPRC for imbalanced data. Domain 8.A is highly relevant for Isolation Forest, autoencoders, and anomaly detection methods. Domain 10.A is highly relevant for federated learning and privacy-preserving approaches. Domains 1-5 (demographics, cultural practices, expense categorization, existing systems, behavioral profiles) were considered but rejected as not primary focus. Domain 7 (algorithm evaluation) was considered but rejected. Domain 9 (mobile app design) was considered but rejected. Domain 11 (other domains) was considered but rejected. Domain 12 (algorithm evaluation) was considered but rejected. Domain 13 (savings/debt) was considered but rejected. Domain 14 (synthetic data) was considered but rejected.
limitations: Review may not capture very recent developments post-2023 in rapidly evolving field.
Case study results from single bank may not represent all financial fraud scenarios.
Focus on transaction-level fraud may miss higher-level organizational fraud patterns.
Performance comparisons may be affected by different preprocessing and feature engineering.
Operational constraints like latency and computational cost not fully addressed.
Ethical considerations of automated fraud detection require more comprehensive treatment.
